stages.title: STAGE 1 — Equal Superposition
stages.objective: Initialize equal superposition across all 4 basis states using Hadamard gates on both wires.
stages.narration: We begin in the ground state |00⟩. By applying a Hadamard gate to qubit 0 and qubit 1, we place both wires into equal superposition. The composite two-qubit state now has an identical probability amplitude of one-half across all four computational basis states: |00⟩, |01⟩, |10⟩, and |11⟩.

stages.objective: Mark target state |11⟩ with a phase flip using a Controlled-Z oracle connection or equivalent H-CX-H decomposition.

stages.narration_pre_pause: The oracle needs to mark state |11⟩ with a phase flip. Which connection completes that?
stages.narration_post_resolved: The oracle is in place. State |11⟩ now carries a negative phase, but because measurement probabilities depend only on the squared magnitude of each amplitude, this phase flip remains invisible to direct readout.

actions.text: The oracle needs to mark state |11⟩ with a phase flip. Which connection completes that?

actions.description: Cursor pauses here. Await learner drag-and-drop or connection of CZ oracle gate (or equivalent H-CX-H sandwich).

actions.text: The marked state now carries a negative phase, invisible to direct measurement. We need an interference step to convert this phase into probability.

stages.title: STAGE 3 — Grover Diffusion Operator
stages.objective: Perform inversion about the mean via H⊗² → X⊗² → CZ → X⊗² → H⊗² to amplify target amplitude to 100%.
stages.narration: Now we apply the Grover diffusion operator: H on both wires, X on both wires, a CZ connection, followed by X and H on both wires. This operation reflects all amplitudes about their mean. Because the mean is positive one-fourth and state |11⟩ was negative one-half, reflection about the mean amplifies the marked state to certainty, while destructively canceling out all other states.

actions.text: Now we construct the diffusion operator: H on both wires, X on both wires, CZ, X on both wires, and H on both wires.
The average amplitude across all four states is exactly one-quarter. Applying inversion about the mean: alpha prime equals two mu minus alpha.
Reflection about the mean amplifies the marked state to certainty, while the unmarked states completely disappear.

stages.title: STAGE 4 — Measurement & Readout
stages.objective: Complete the predict-iteration assessment gate, measure computational basis wires over 1000 shots, and verify P(|11⟩) ≈ 0.99–1.00.

assessment_gate.question: For this 2-qubit search space (N = 4 items) with 1 marked state, how many Grover iterations (Oracle + Diffusion) are required to reach peak target probability?
assessment_gate.explanation: For N = 4, the rotation angle per Grover step is theta = pi/3. Exactly 1 iteration places the state vector completely on the marked state (|11⟩) with 100% theoretical probability. A second iteration would over-rotate the vector to 150 degrees, dropping the target probability back down to ~25% and returning all four outcomes to ~25% uniform probability.

stages.narration_pre_checkpoint: Before we run the simulation: based on the amplitude amplification formula, predict the optimal number of Grover iterations needed for this four-item search space.
stages.narration_post_checkpoint: Exactly one iteration. For N equals four, a single rotation achieves one hundred percent theoretical probability. Now let's measure both wires and run one thousand shots on the simulator.
